item.text: {"findings":[{"claim":"Recommendation: use built-in fetch for this bounded CLI. Add explicit HTTP-status handling, JSON parsing, and a signal combining cancellation with a deadline. Axios remains reasonable if an existing shared client already supplies useful error conventions. This is an engineering inference, supported by the [Node.js migration guidance](https://nodejs.org/learn/userland-migrations/axios-to-whatwg-fetch), rather than a performance finding.","source_url":"https://nodejs.org/learn/userland-migrations/axios-to-whatwg-fetch","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"nodejs-official","proposed_tier":"T2_inferred","falsifier":"A required deployment environment or endpoint needs behavior that fetch cannot provide within acceptable implementation cost, or existing Axios integration makes migration more costly than retaining it.","limitations":["Documentation and source review only; no code, installations, modifications, or runtime tests were performed. All proposed tiers are advisory.","Existing Axios usage, proxy requirements, private certificate authorities, response sizes, and precise deadline semantics are unspecified.","No Windows, macOS, or Linux compatibility matrix or performance comparison was executed."]},{"claim":"Fetch is a stable global API in both Node.js 22 and 24: it stopped requiring an enabling flag in Node 18 and became non-experimental in Node 21. Ordinary use needs no fetch package or import. See the [Node 22 documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#fetch) and [Node 24 documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#fetch).","source_url":"https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#fetch","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"nodejs-official","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"A standard, unmodified Node.js 22 or 24 installation lacks global fetch under its normal launch configuration.","limitations":["Availability was checked in versioned documentation, not running binaries.","Custom builds, embedded runtimes, launch flags, and supported OS versions or architectures were not surveyed.","The two Node.js documentation pages are not independent sources."]},{"claim":"Fetch does not reject solely because an HTTP response has a 4xx or 5xx status. A GET helper must inspect response.ok or response.status and deliberately create its HTTP error behavior; catch alone is insufficient. [Node.js migration notes](https://nodejs.org/learn/userland-migrations/axios-to-whatwg-fetch#notes).","source_url":"https://nodejs.org/learn/userland-migrations/axios-to-whatwg-fetch#notes","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"nodejs-official","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"Unwrapped fetch rejects a successfully received, otherwise valid 404 or 500 response solely because of its status.","limitations":["Network failures, cancellation, and body-parsing failures are separate error paths.","The brief does not specify acceptable statuses, error-body retention, or the CLI's error format."]},{"claim":"Axios rejects HTTP responses outside 200–299 by default. Its error.response exposes the response data, status, and headers; validateStatus can change which statuses reject. This provides a ready-made HTTP error convention. [Axios error handling](https://axios.rest/pages/advanced/error-handling).","source_url":"https://axios.rest/pages/advanced/error-handling","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"axios-official","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"An uncustomized Axios request resolves a final 404 or 500 response instead of rejecting.","limitations":["Instance defaults, custom adapters, and validateStatus overrides can change behavior.","A connection failure need not contain error.response; HTTP and transport failures still require distinct handling."]},{"claim":"Node.js supplies the deadline/cancellation primitives needed by either client: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) creates a timed signal, and AbortSignal.any([userSignal, deadlineSignal]) aborts when either input aborts and preserves the triggering reason. Both APIs predate Node 22. [Node.js AbortSignal documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#static-method-abortsignalanysignals).","source_url":"https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#static-method-abortsignalanysignals","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"nodejs-official","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"The composed signal fails to abort when either constituent signal aborts, or does not preserve the triggering reason as documented.","limitations":["The CLI must connect its user-cancellation event to an AbortController.","The deadline starts when the timed signal is created; the intended start point and timeout duration are unspecified.","Timer-based deadlines are not exact scheduling guarantees: [Node.js timers](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.0.0/docs/api/timers.html#settimeoutcallback-delay-args)."]},{"claim":"Fetch cancellation remains relevant after response headers arrive: Node's implementation connects the signal to the fetch operation and response body. Therefore, keep the deadline active through the awaited body read, rather than stopping it when fetch first resolves. [Node.js fetch implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.0.0/deps/undici/src/lib/web/fetch/index.js).","source_url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.0.0/deps/undici/src/lib/web/fetch/index.js","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"official-source-code-on-raw.githubusercontent.com","proposed_tier":"T2_inferred","falsifier":"A response sends headers immediately and then stalls its body, but aborting the attached signal leaves the pending body read running successfully.","limitations":["Inferred from the Node 24.0.0 implementation; delayed-body behavior was not exercised across Node patches or operating systems.","This does not establish preemption of synchronous JSON parsing.","GitHub-hosted source files share one origin group; project source and its own documentation are also not independent corroboration."]},{"claim":"Axios supports AbortController through its signal option in Node.js, with support introduced in Axios 0.22.0. It can therefore receive the composed user/deadline signal. Its older CancelToken API is deprecated. [Axios cancellation documentation](https://axios.rest/pages/advanced/cancellation).","source_url":"https://axios.rest/pages/advanced/cancellation","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"axios-official","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"A supported Axios version using its standard Node adapter ignores cancellation from the supplied AbortSignal.","limitations":["The project's intended Axios version and adapter are unspecified.","Passing a composed signal is an inference from Axios accepting AbortSignal and Node documenting signal composition.","Cancellation races and application-specific error classification were not tested."]},{"claim":"Axios defaults timeout to 0, meaning no configured timeout. Its Node HTTP adapter delegates timeout handling to the transport and includes connection-phase handling; this should not be treated as a universal deadline through completion of the response body. Use an explicit deadline signal when that is the requirement. [Axios defaults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/lib/defaults/index.js), [HTTP adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/lib/adapters/http.js).","source_url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/lib/adapters/http.js","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"official-source-code-on-raw.githubusercontent.com","proposed_tier":"T2_inferred","falsifier":"The selected adapter demonstrably maintains one elapsed-time timeout across connection, redirects, and the complete body, including continuously arriving slow chunks.","limitations":["Source inspection covers Axios 1.20.0; other versions and adapters may differ.","DNS delays, TLS stalls, redirects, and slow-body scenarios were not tested.","The brief does not distinguish an inactivity timeout from an overall elapsed-time deadline."]},{"claim":"Fetch requires an explicit await response.json(). Node's implementation fully reads the body and parses it with JSON.parse, rejecting malformed JSON; an empty body also fails JSON parsing. [Node.js JSON body implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.0.0/deps/undici/src/lib/web/fetch/body.js).","source_url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.0.0/deps/undici/src/lib/web/fetch/body.js","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"official-source-code-on-raw.githubusercontent.com","proposed_tier":"T2_inferred","falsifier":"An unread, unmodified Response containing malformed or empty JSON resolves response.json() successfully.","limitations":["Successful JSON parsing does not validate the application's expected data shape.","The CLI needs an explicit policy for 204 responses and other empty bodies.","Response-size limits and memory consumption were not assessed; synchronous parsing is not interruptible by a timer callback."]},{"claim":"Axios automatically attempts JSON parsing, but malformed JSON can remain a string under its default permissive behavior. For nonempty malformed JSON to reject, set responseType to 'json' and transitional.silentJSONParsing to false. [Axios 1.20.0 response transformation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/lib/defaults/index.js).","source_url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/lib/defaults/index.js","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"official-source-code-on-raw.githubusercontent.com","proposed_tier":"T2_inferred","falsifier":"With the standard response transform, the stated strict settings accept nonempty malformed JSON, or default permissive parsing invariably rejects it.","limitations":["Empty strings bypass the implementation's parsing branch even with these strict settings.","Custom response transforms can change the result; parsed data still needs application validation.","The [configuration documentation](https://axios.rest/pages/advanced/request-config#transitional) mentions null for silent failures, while the inspected tagged implementation returns the original data. This finding follows the implementation."]},{"claim":"Built-in fetch uses Node's bundled Undici and adds no HTTP-client package dependency. Axios adds a separately managed package; its 1.20.0 manifest declares follow-redirects, form-data, https-proxy-agent, and proxy-from-env as runtime dependencies. [Node.js fetch documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.0.0/docs/api/globals.html#fetch), [Axios package manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/package.json).","source_url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axios/axios/v1.20.0/package.json","source_kind":"primary_authoritative","retrieved_at":"2026-10-14","independence_group":"official-source-code-on-raw.githubusercontent.com","proposed_tier":"T3_observed","falsifier":"Ordinary built-in fetch requires installing an HTTP-client package, or the cited Axios manifest does not declare those runtime dependencies.","limitations":["Dependency count alone does not establish comparative security, reliability, speed, or installation size.","The resolved transitive dependency tree and any existing dependency deduplication are unknown.","Bundled Undici still requires maintenance through Node updates; using built-in fetch does not eliminate underlying HTTP-client code."]}]}
